candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: With five dimensional variables (rho, mu, D, U, epsilon) and three fundamental base dimensions (mass M, length L, time T), Buckingham Pi gives 5-3=2 independent dimensionless groups. The physically relevant groups are the Reynolds number Re = rho*U*D/mu and the relative roughness epsilon/D. Therefore the (dimensionless) Darcy-Weisbach friction factor f_D must be a function of these two groups: f_D = F(Re, epsilon/D). This leads to the familiar implicit Colebrook-type relationship in turbulent flow and to explicit laminar expressions when roughness or Reynolds-number effects dominate.

If a correction remains partly unknown, preserve null and explain what remains unresolved; the program will request revision rather than invent zeros. Lack of KB alone is not a physical contradiction. Matrix compilation and n/r/k are program tasks, not audit tasks.

final_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: With five dimensional variables (rho, mu, D, U, epsilon) and three fundamental base dimensions (mass M, length L, time T), Buckingham Pi gives 5-3=2 independent dimensionless groups. The physically relevant groups are the Reynolds number Re = rho*U*D/mu and the relative roughness epsilon/D. Therefore the (dimensionless) Darcy-Weisbach friction factor f_D must be a function of these two groups: f_D = F(Re, epsilon/D). This leads to the familiar implicit Colebrook-type relationship in turbulent flow and to explicit laminar expressions when roughness or Reynolds-number effects dominate.
